message.content: Give me a set of things to test

content.text:
Here's a test plan, ordered so each stage builds on the last. Stages 1–2 are quick sanity; 3–6 are the ones that can actually surprise us, because the unit tests fake the harness payloads — a real Claude Code session is the thing I couldn't verify from here.

## 1. Install & init (fresh repo)

- [ ] `./install.sh` → `sun` on PATH (`~/.local/bin`); `sun` with no args prints usage, not a traceback
- [ ] `sun init` in an empty dir: creates git repo, `.git/sun/`, `.claude/settings.json` with hooks on all 5 events **without a matcher**
- [ ] `sun init` in a repo with existing `.claude/settings.json` hooks: your hooks are preserved, `sun hook` appended once; run it twice → no duplicates
- [ ] `sun init` in a dirty repo → one `sun: initial state` commit attributed to you
- [ ] Any `sun` command outside an initialized repo → clean error, exit non-zero

## 2. CLI commands (scriptable, but eyeball the output)

- [ ] Edit a file by hand → `sun log` commits it as `[human:<you>]` with your git `user.name`
- [ ] `sun show <commit>` on: a sun commit, a manual `git commit` (should say "no sun operations recorded"), and a short hash
- [ ] `sun undo` → latest op reverted; `sun undo --op <id>` after later touching the same lines → refuses atomically (files unchanged)
- [ ] `sun undo --commit HEAD` on a merge commit
- [ ] `sun viz` → open in browser: chips, replay slider, per-actor % bar, patch detail pane. Check it on the 41MB `sundial.html` too — does the browser survive?

## 3. Real Claude Code session ← highest value

This is the part the unit tests simulate. In a `sun init`-ed repo, start a real session:

- [ ] Ask Claude to edit 2–3 files with Edit/Write in one turn → after the turn: **one** `sun: agent:… turn N (k tool calls)` commit on the branch, per-call commits visible via `git log --all` / `sun show`
- [ ] Check `events.jsonl`: is `tool_call_id` populated? (If null everywhere, your CC version doesn't send `tool_use_id` — attribution still works, but tell me and I'll parse it from elsewhere)
- [ ] Ask Claude to edit a file **via Bash** (`sed -i`, `cat >`) → event should be `agent`, `method: hook_diff` — not human
- [ ] Edit a file yourself **while Claude is mid-turn** → your edit gets its own `human` event; agent's turn unaffected
- [ ] Ask Claude to spawn **parallel subagents** that both edit files → each edit attributed, no leaked entries in `.git/sun/active.json` afterwards
- [ ] A turn where Claude only reads/greps (no edits) → no commits, no junk events
- [ ] Interrupt a turn mid-tool-call (Esc) → next `sun` command doesn't misattribute or wedge; `active.json` eventually empty
- [ ] Two Claude sessions in two terminals on the same repo at once → interleaved commits, correct actors, no squash-folding of each other's work

## 4. Attribution edge cases

- [ ] Human edits the **same file** the agent is editing, same turn → whose event wins, and does the result match your intuition? (Current rule: for Edit/Write tools the named file is 100% agent's)
- [ ] File **deletion** and **rename** by the agent — do events/patches look right?
- [ ] Filenames with spaces / unicode
- [ ] Human edits on a **non-main branch** and detached HEAD → commit lands where you were
- [ ] A manual `git commit` mid-agent-turn → squash correctly skipped, per-call commits remain

## 5. Durability

- [ ] `git gc --prune=now` after several turns → `sun show <per-call-commit>` still works
- [ ] `git push` / `pull` on a sun repo — confirm `refs/sun/*` don't get pushed unexpectedly (they shouldn't by default; check your push config)
- [ ] Kill a `sun hook` process mid-write (`kill -9`) → next command recovers (torn `events.jsonl` lines are skipped by design)
- [ ] `sun` commands from a **subdirectory** of the repo

## 6. Known gaps to confirm you're OK with

- [ ] Old repos initialised before this change still have matcher-scoped hooks (Bash edits → human) until you delete the old entries and re-run `sun init`
- [ ] Concurrent-agent turns never squash → busy repos accumulate per-call commits on the branch — acceptable?
- [ ] `sun log` shows human overlays that followed a squash on the turn commit — is that display what you want?

If you run stage 3 and paste me the resulting `events.jsonl` (or any weirdness), I can fix whatever the real payloads break.
